--- title: "September 23, 2026" date: 2026-09-23 description: "Network median 0.08 in (range 0.00–2.36 in); peak IVT 68 kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹ from the SW" categories: [IVT < 250, Final] execute: freeze: auto --- ## Summary Most of the rain fell between Wednesday morning and afternoon, September 23, over about 4 hours. Rain gauges across Flagstaff caught a typical 0.08 inches, from 0.00 in at Rio de Flag at Butler to 2.36 in at Peak View Park. The airport measured 0.12 in, about 2 times the normal for the day. Moist air flowing from the southwest was lifted by an area of low pressure aloft centred about 660 miles to the southwest, but the flow of moisture stayed below atmospheric-river strength. ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Technical summary Across 37 gauges the event total ranged from 0.00 to 2.36 in (median 0.08 in). The central 80% of the network-mean rain fell between Sep 23 11:00 MST and Sep 23 15:00 MST (4 h). Moisture transport over Flagstaff stayed below atmospheric-river strength: ERA5 IVT peaked at 68 kg m⁻¹ s⁻¹ from the SW at Sep 23 05:00 MST, and total column water vapour reached 18 mm. At the IVT peak, 500-hPa flow over Flagstaff was from the SW at 9 m s⁻¹, and the 500-hPa trough axis along 35.25°N was at 115.2°W, 327 km west of Flagstaff (5,824 m, against 5,834 m over Flagstaff). A closed 500-hPa low (5,815 m) was centred 1,060 km to the SW, at 28.0°N 119.0°W. The strongest 250-hPa wind within 1,000 km was 49 m s⁻¹, 887 km to the NNE. The 250-hPa wind over Flagstaff peaked at 31 m s⁻¹ (Sep 23 05:00 MST), at the same time as the IVT peak. ::: ## Rain across the network ::: {#e9a0628d .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Event rain total at each city and county gauge (circle color and label show the total in inches; map cropped to the network) over shaded relief (USGS 3DEP), 200-m elevation contours, streams (USGS NHD) and highways (Census TIGER). Tap or click the map to open the frame full size.* ## What the forecasters said The National Weather Service office in Flagstaff discussed the moisture source in its Area Forecast Discussions as the event unfolded. Excerpts, quoted verbatim (links to the Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive): - **Sep 23, 2:56 AM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202609230956)): "A significant plume of deep monsoon moisture continues to flow northward into New Mexico, with widespread rain and thunderstorms. Over northern Arizona, drier air remains for much of Coconino/Yavapai counties early this morning, with dewpoints in the 30s/40s." - **Sep 23, 12:14 PM MST** ([AFD](https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=AFDFGZ&e=202609231914)): "Moisture continues to stream into Arizona, as deep and layered southwest flow persists over the southwest United States. The bulk of the moisture resides in New Mexico, but outflows are pushing higher dew points into portions of eastern, southern and central Arizona this afternoon." ## Climate context - **Airport precipitation:** 0.12 in over 1 local day, against a 1991–2020 normal of 0.05 in for those days (2× normal). - **Rank:** the 117th largest 1-day airport total in September among 129 years with data since 1898 (each year's largest 1-day total ending in September). - **Airport temperature:** highs averaged +0.0 °F and lows +4.0 °F relative to normal. - **Water year to date** (Oct 1, 2025 – Sep 23, 2026): airport 19.6 in (97% of normal); SNOTEL Fort Valley 18.2 in (100% of median); Snowslide Canyon 36.3 in (105% of median); Fry 29.6 in (116% of median). ## Station data **Flagstaff airport** (local days; normals 1991–2020; M = not yet reported) | | Precip (in) | Normal (in) | Snow (in) | High (°F) | High vs normal | Low (°F) | Low vs normal | |:-------|--------------:|--------------:|------------:|------------:|-----------------:|-----------:|----------------:| | Sep 23 | 0.12 | 0.05 | 0 | 72 | +0 | 44 | +4 | | Total | 0.12 | 0.05 | 0 | | | | | **SNOTEL** (water-year precipitation from Oct 1; medians 1991–2020) | site | Event precip (in) | Water-year precip (in) | Median to date (in) | % of median | SWE at end (in) | Max snow depth (in) | |:-----------------|--------------------:|-------------------------:|----------------------:|--------------:|------------------:|----------------------:| | Fort Valley | 0 | 18.2 | 18.2 | 100 | 0 | 0 | | Snowslide Canyon | 0.3 | 36.3 | 34.7 | 105 | 0 | 0 | | Fry | 0.1 | 29.6 | 25.5 | 116 | 0 | 0 |
